summary: Prepare for forward deployed and solutions engineering roles: discovering customer problems, building integrations fast, working with data and APIs, and explaining trade-offs.

topics.title: Discovery with customers
topics.why: The best answers show you found the real problem.
points: Asking about the last time the problem happened
Separating the request from the need

topics.title: Working with data
points: Building a small pipeline that can be re-run

topics.title: Building with AI models
topics.why: Many forward deployed roles now involve AI.

topics.title: Explaining trade-offs
topics.why: Interviewers test how you talk to non-engineers.

exercises.title: Integrate two APIs
steps: In your code editor, write a small script that reads from one public API and writes to another (or a file).
Handle errors, retries and a rate limit.
Record a 3-minute walkthrough explaining your choices and what you'd do for a real customer.

exercises.title: Clean a messy dataset
steps: Take a public CSV with missing and inconsistent values.
Clean it with SQL or Python and write checks that fail on bad data.
Record yourself explaining the problems you found and how you handled them.

exercises.title: Build a small AI assistant for a 'customer'
exercises.goal: Show you can ship with AI.
steps: Pick a pretend customer problem (for example summarising support tickets).
Build a small prototype with your AI model of choice, including a simple evaluation.
Record a demo and a one-minute explanation of the trade-offs, as if to a director.

practice.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
practice.summary: Practice interview for a forward deployed engineer: customer discovery, building in the field, data and APIs, explaining trade-offs.

anchors.3: Finds the real need and adjusts.
anchors.5: Uncovers a different underlying problem and aligns stakeholders.

competencies.name: Building and shipping
competencies.description: Ships working solutions under real constraints.

anchors.3: Ships a solution and solves a real obstacle.
anchors.5: Ships under real constraints with measured results.

competencies.name: Data and APIs
competencies.description: Works confidently with APIs and messy data.

anchors.3: Describes integrating an API or cleaning data.
anchors.5: Describes reliable integrations with retries, checks and monitoring.

anchors.3: Explains a choice so a non-engineer can decide.
anchors.5: Adapts for audiences and reaches a decision everyone understands.

questions.text: Tell me about a time a customer asked for one thing but needed something else. How did you find out?
Tell me about something you built and shipped for a customer. What got in the way?
Imagine a customer's data arrives with duplicates and missing fields every night. How would you handle it?
How would you explain to a director the choice between a quick fix and a robust solution?
Tell me about a time you had to learn a new technology quickly to help a customer.

practice.company_facts: This is a practice interview. There is no real employer: questions about pay, hours or the team can't be answered here.

settings.next_steps: Your coaching feedback appears as soon as the interview ends.
